about: Every way money may cross between the town and the outside world in a played year, and the record that matches it (money stress audit defect 3). A journal entry touching an outside account must match one row by its source kind and, for accounts transfers, the transfer id's leading segment. A row marked plug is a stand-in the dollar test rejects; any flow matching no row is rejected too.

flows.what: Counted households' purchases from outside sellers and pay from outside employers, through the residents engine's pooled account.
An official's salary for days in office, from the government that seats them (official-pay).
Unemployment benefits paid under the state's law to a claimant.
A counted household moving away takes its share of the pool with it.
Building work bought from outside contractors.
Mortgage payments to an outside lender.
Rent passed to landlords who live outside the town.
A recorded finance contract (supplies, services) settled with an outside party.
A buyer outside the town paying a household for the home its owners sold on leaving; the lender is paid off from the price first.
What a sold home brought beyond its mortgage payoff, paid by the outside buyer to the household.
Buyers outside the town paying a town business for its goods and services (the outside market).
A town business paying outside suppliers for what it uses.
Wages from an employer outside the town for recorded work.
Social Security retirement awards paid under federal law to a claimant.
A business's cash above its cushion paid to its outside owner.
A branch's retained earnings swept to its parent company.
What is left of a business closed by choice, paid to its owner.
An heirless estate escheating to the decedent's state, or an inheritance to an heir outside the town (estates.ts).
A counted household moving in brings its cash from the outside market into its group (the mirror of counted-departure).
A full household moving away takes its cash out of town (moves).
A counted entrant's pay from outside employers and purchases from outside sellers, kept as the same recorded flows the household it takes the shape of already had (residents-economy).
A price-rule change in what households and businesses pay outside sellers for a good (energy, fuel), settled in place-prices.
Property tax a household owes under the law in force, paid to a government whose books are outside the town (housing-property-tax).
The federal treasury's monthly borrowing from outside to cover its gap, part of the same stand-in as outside-revenue.
A treasury's even twelfth of each spending line paid to outside payees (and in-town businesses), part of the same stand-in as outside-revenue.
A twelfth of a government's yearly Census revenue paid in each month with no taxpayer, sale or grant behind it.
